problems_found: STATISTIC MISMATCH in sec4b AR(1) stacked-peak nulls (reproduced defect, not a nuance). The null is built as (1/22)*sum_p max_f P_p,r(f) (mean of per-pass maxima) while the observed statistic is max_f (1/22)*sum_p P_p(f) (max of pass-means). I reproduced the track's null exactly with my own code (q50 0.24297 vs reported 0.24247, q95 0.2672 vs 0.26988 for model A), and the correctly matched null is ~1.7x smaller (max-of-pass-mean q50 0.0412 / q95 0.0965 / q99 0.1053 for A). Consequence: the reported p_stacked_global_peak_vs_ar1 A=0.9967, B=1.0, C=1.0 are all wrong; with a matched AR(1) null A and B have p<0.004 (0/300) and C has p=0.0267. The same mismatch applies to the band-limited variant: reported p_vs_matched_ar1_null A=1.0, C=0.994 vs recomputed 0.185 (A) and 0.065 (C). These p-values are in the machine-readable output and read as 'the stacked peaks are red-noise consistent'; under a correct null they are significant excesses.

MISLABELED NULL. sec4b phase_randomised_stacked_null is called 'periodogram-preserving (circular time shift)', but with irregular 1-minute sampling held fixed a circular shift is a time translation, not a phase randomisation; I measured the normalized LS power change over shifts: median max-relative change 0.275, worst pass 0.810 (pass_19), >0.4 for 12 of 22 passes. The null is not what the label and purpose text claim, although its stacked p for the global peak (A 0.00333) does reproduce with a matched statistic.

STATED VERDICT CLAUSE FALSE FOR MODEL B. 'pass-level 860-1310 uHz band power is consistent with an AR(1) red-noise null in all three models' is wrong for B: median per-pass percentile 0.0085, 0 of 22 passes above the median, two-sided sign test p=4.8e-7, and the out-of-sample split-half check is the same (observed ratio median 0.211 vs null percentile 0.0085, sign test p=4.8e-7). B's band power is a reproducible DEFICIT relative to AR(1); the AR(1) null fails for B (opposite sign from, but equally inconsistent as, model C's marginal excess). The track computed these numbers but never flagged the inconsistency.

INVALID CHANCE NULL for the reported 'pass-peak support' number. expected_passes_by_chance_fixed=3.315 assumes uniformly distributed pass-peak frequencies; the proper red-noise full-pipeline null gives 8.29 per 22 passes (95% interval 4-12) for model A, 4.62 (2-8) B, 5.30 (2-9) C. So the reported 16/22 (A) appears more extreme than a red-noise null supports. Moreover A's support is explained by broadband low-frequency excess, not by a line: the stacked peak is only 1.16x the local median within 1 resolution element, and per-pass peak frequencies are broadly spread (median 557 uHz, IQR 432-656).

METADATA CONTRADICTION in the output: sec4b phase_randomised_stacked_null top-level 'n_realisations': 500 while the per-model values (and the executed loop, n_sh=300) are 300; the script comment says 500. A consumer reading the top-level field is misled about the null resolution (1/500 vs 1/300).

BOUNDARY-FRAGILE COUNTS. Model C's 'passes above the AR(1) 99th percentile = 1/22' and '3/22 above q95' rest on percentiles estimated from 1000 surrogates; pass_03 model C has band percentile 0.949 (track) / 0.9565, 0.947, 0.9465, 0.9495 across four independent 1000-surrogate seeds, so the q95 count varies 3-4 of 22 across seeds. The quoted counts should carry a Monte-Carlo tolerance; the underlying conclusion (no strong line) is unaffected.

Not found (checked and absent): no p-value or CI anywhere treats the 1698 time samples or grid rows as independent - every sign test, Wilcoxon and KS in the JSON is aggregated at the 22-pass level, and sec5's uniform-phase null is a legitimate chance null; no cartesian-grid claim; no physical-uniqueness claim from information criteria; no asserted number without a code path reproducing it. I re-ran track2_spectral_tests.py in a sandbox copy on the same data: exit 0, 1127 s, and a full recursive numeric diff against output/results/spectral_tests.json gave exactly one difference (/runtime_sec 508.14 vs 1127.08), i.e. every substantive number is bit-for-bit reproducible. The band/percentile null result is not a bug: my entirely independent LS + lfilter pipeline reproduces the null findings (no in-band stacked peak for A or B, band percentiles near/below the middle for A and B, model C marginal), and the AR(1) surrogates are drawn independently of the observed series.
